content.thinking:
I need to plan out the whole scene carefully before writing anything. I'm thinking through the koala's realistic proportions and how it would be posed clinging to a eucalyptus branch stand, with a base plinth supporting a forked vertical trunk where the koala sits gripping the wood.

I'm settling on a Y-shaped wooden stand: a vertical trunk leaning to one side rising to a horizontal branch, with a shorter fork branch in front for the koala's hands to grip while its hips rest on the main branch, facing forward.

Adding leaves on the sprig and working out overall proportions: plinth and branch heights, koala sitting height to around 0.85 with the sprig reaching 0.95, matching realistic koala body proportions. Now I'm setting up the skeleton hierarchy starting with hips at the root, then spine segments up through neck and head, with a slight lean for a natural sitting pose.

Defining the spine chain joints...

Adding head joint with forward-facing orientation, then a jaw joint parented to it — I'll stick with explicit absolute positions and bone assignments rather than local coordinate math to avoid roll errors.

Building out the skull, muzzle, and nose geometry as scaled spheres with blocky box proportions to keep the pixel-art aesthetic consistent.

For fur, I'm settling on a cell-painting texel size of 0.015-0.016m, calculating texture density so each fur cell spans roughly 7 texels for a clean blocky look, and using low-poly flat-shaded spheres to avoid smooth shading that would break the pixel style.

Now I'm figuring out eye placement using thin textured boxes embedded into the head sphere's surface, positioning them based on the skull's radius and orientation.

Good enough margin there. I'll simplify the head geometry using scaled spheres with modest segment counts for a flat-faceted low-poly look, then move to fur shading: a gray ramp with speckled randomness for the body and a lighter countershaded belly based on vertical position.

Writing fur paint logic...

For the body shape, I'm lofting a pear-like form along the spine chain with varying elliptical radii—wider at the hips and belly, narrowing toward the chest and neck—and adding rounded caps at each end.

I'm positioning the koala's bum to bulge naturally over the branch, nudging the hip joint up to around y=0.50 so the bottom curve sits just above the branch surface at 0.395, then shifting the whole spine chain upward accordingly: hips, torso points, neck joint, and head center all stacked with the head topping out near y=0.95.

Working out the head geometry now - setting the skull's scaled radii and figuring out eye placement relative to the head center, planning to use a scaled sphere for the skull shape and compute eye coordinates as offsets from that center point.

Still computing eye position math...

Now thinking through the neck-to-body connection, considering sweeping a tube along the spine chain through to the head base to join them smoothly.

Now I'm placing the head skull center near the top of the neck, then working out shoulder, elbow, and hand positions for the arms so the hands converge on the sprig held in front of the chest.

Checking the arm length against my IK limb segments confirms the reach is feasible, so I'm setting a bend hint so the elbow points outward and slightly down, keeping the limb in the plane formed by the shoulder, hand target, and that hint vector. I'm using the sign of the side (left positive X, right negative X) to mirror joint placement and naming conventions like shoulderL and shoulderR consistently.

Now I'm working out the hand anatomy — koala hands have opposable thumbs with a 3+2 digit split, so I'll build each hand as short two-joint finger chains plus thumb chains, parented to the nearest spine joint near the shoulder height, so the fingers can wrap around a gripped sprig in the rest pose.

Still placing finger coordinates...

Each hand gets 3 finger chains of 3 joints each, wrapping from a tip point near the wrist outward, giving 9 joints per hand and 18 total across both paws, with tapering dark gray tubes and simple box tips instead of separate claw shapes.

I'll offset left and right hands' y-position slightly for a natural look, then build the palm as a sphere attached to the wrist joint and sweep the arm into a fur-covered tube using the chain's parent-child bone structure.

Now I'm working out leg placement for the sitting pose, positioning hips, thighs, and knees so the hind legs wrap forward and down with feet gripping the top of the branch.

Now I'm working out the hind foot placement on the branch, with toes curling around its front surface as a chain of points wrapping down from the top contact point.

Adding the vertical trunk and a second thinner offshoot, plus a connecting twig curving from the branch toward a sprig that wasn't properly touching before.

Right, static parts without their own bone need to attach to a joint, so I'll just assign them all to the hips as the rig's root. Actually it might be cleaner to add a dedicated "base" joint near the floor and make hips a child of that, giving the stand its own stable root separate from the spine.

Now I'm working out the bark coloring for the wood branches — a warm tan-to-cream ramp with occasional green tint patches to mimic eucalyptus bark, plus streak patterns running along the trunk direction.

Then I'm sizing the base plinth: a wood box sized to fit the koala and sprig layout, roughly 0.95 x 0.06 x 0.6, keeping the z-extent aligned with the sprig placement.

Working out the plank texture...

I'm thinking about adding small decorative details like corner rivets and a tiny front plaque, maybe with a simple leaf icon instead of text since letters would be too complex at this pixel scale. Now moving on to the trunk structure, planning a vertical rod positioned off-center.

Still writing branch geometry...

Adding leaf cards along the twig...

Still writing leaf pixel shaping...

I'm adding two leaf color variants plus small gumnut capsules on the twig using brown-capped spheres. For the koala, I'm planning fur paint details: gray dithered body, lighter cream belly, dark fingers on hands and feet, and a face with lighter muzzle, black nose, and fluffy white-interior ears.

Now I'm working out ear geometry: a flattened gray outer ellipsoid for the outside, a smaller cream ellipsoid offset forward for the inner fluff, and a ring of small cream tufts around the rim built from boxes arranged in a circle facing outward from the ear center.

Still shaping the ears...

Now placing the muzzle and nose - working out a big black bulb nose sitting atop the muzzle front, with a tiny cream highlight box nudged just outside the nose's ellipsoid surface for a glossy pixel-art touch.

For the mouth, I'm positioning a cream lower jaw ellipsoid beneath the muzzle and a thin dark slit box for the mouth line, adjusting the muzzle's vertical placement so it doesn't overlap the jaw. I'm also adding cream cheek tuft spheres on either side of the face for texture.

Now I'm designing tiny pixel-art eyes using a small grid pattern with dark pixels and a white glint, placed symmetrically on the face, and considering fur tuft cards scattered across the head and body using a small gray pixel texture for added detail.

Defining the tuft pixel pattern...

Skipping the joey idea, I'm deciding the belly bulge is already covered by the sweep radius. Now I'm defining the spine chain points curving from the hips up toward the shoulders to set up the bone hierarchy.

For the body sweep, I'm working out a radius function along the spine that varies width and depth at each point to shape the torso, trying to figure out how to interpolate those radius values since only a static circle size is exported by the sweep builder.

Going with smooth skin for the body. Checking the bottom cap placement so the body sinks slightly into the branch and looks properly seated rather than floating.

Now setting up the neck joint chain and head joint hierarchy, with the jaw as a child of the head for articulation. I'm assigning body parts to their bone chains, starting with shoulder spheres where the arms attach.

Checking the shoulder position against the body radius to make sure it sits at the edge correctly, then working out the IK arm chain by computing the distance from shoulder root to hand target.

Still computing elbow bend geometry...

Now I'm setting the palm sphere position and defining finger digit chains with proper naming, then adding the finger sweep geometry with rounded caps in the hand color before moving on to the hip joint for the legs.

For the legs, I'm placing the hip joint and computing the foot target on the branch, checking that the short reach relative to the long limb segments creates a highly bent knee—working out the knee position by offsetting perpendicular to the hip-foot line using the sweep direction.

Still calculating knee position...

Placing toes now, three per foot spaced along x, curling down to grip the branch's top surface which sits around y=0.397 at the branch edges.

For claws, I'm adding a small spike at the tip of the last finger using the final chain point and direction, giving it a cream color to look like a tiny nail.

Now I'm moving to surface details like ear tufts, cheek fur, and brow, scattering small fur cards across the head sphere surface while excluding the front face area so it stays clean.

Then I'm figuring out tuft card sizing and texture tinting, plus extending the stand with moss patches, pebbles, leaf litter, and bark knots for a more natural eucalyptus branch base.

Now I'm adding a sawn stub coming off the trunk with a flat cut end rendered as a small ringed-texture disc, to suggest a trimmed branch.

Designing more pixel texture rings...

Designing the plaque texture with a gilded rim and darker interior plus small leaf marks, keeping within the flat color budget since textures don't count toward the palette limit. Now sketching the wood base plank texture with horizontal rows for the top surface.

Still writing fur coloring logic...

Defining fur color palettes...

I want to standardize sweep calls to use an options object with color, and I'm sketching an ellipsoid helper for head parts that builds spheres with flat-shaded normals, scaled per mesh while bones stay unscaled.

I'm reasoning through normal correctness for painted spheres under non-uniform scale, assuming the SDK handles baking properly, and confirming types for color (string or Paint) work across surfaces -- whether it's a skull part or a body sweep used for cards.

I'm writing a leaves helper that samples points along a sweep at even intervals with rotating angles, then places leaf cards at each point with randomized size, lean, bend, and flow settings seeded by an rng. I'm checking that the flow vector gets flattened correctly onto the sweep's plane.

Now I'm thinking about adding tip leaves at the end of a branch with zero lean, and considering how eucalyptus leaves naturally droop at branch ends due to the downward-flattened flow direction. I'm also starting to define leaf textures with a palette of greens and blue-greens for the two leaf variants.

Writing leaf texture function...

Adding gumnut spheres to the twigs...

I'm also scattering small dark knots along the trunk sweep and adding pale bark-peel slivers as thin boxes oriented outward along the branch normals.

Now I'm adding flat peeled-bark patches as thin plates lying against the surface, colored in cream and olive tones, keeping the total palette under the color budget before moving on to the trunk's base paint layer.

For bark, I'm stretching the sample point vertically so noise streaks run along the trunk's length, then blending two noise fields to pick a bark ramp color, with rare dark fissure specks and a secondary moss-green patch variation layered in.

Now I'm finalizing the module imports, making sure only the actually-used helpers from builder, frame, ik, math, paint, path, sweep, and the pixel/paint utilities are included to avoid unused-import errors.

Writing meta and build code...

Setting up the hip joint and spine chain...

Defining head and jaw joints, then setting up profile functions for the body sweep's radius variation along the spine.

Writing the ell helper function...

Defining skull and muzzle shapes...

Now adding nose, cheeks with cream fur paint, chin/jaw ellipsoid, and a mouth slit box attached to the head bone.

Next I'm positioning the two eye boxes symmetrically along x, adjusting their y/z offsets relative to the skull center, tilting them slightly outward, and considering a darker fur patch around each eye.

Since a dark eye-patch ellipse would overlap and hide the eye box, I decide to skip it and instead give the eye texture itself a dark surrounding ring using a small pixel grid, keeping the eye box compact. I'm now working out the ear placement, positioning each ear symmetrically at the top sides of the skull where it meets the skull's upper boundary.

Each ear gets an outer fur-colored ellipse and an inner cream-colored ellipse offset along the ear's facing direction, plus a ring of small alternating-colored tuft boxes arranged around the rim to give a textured edge, using item index parity to vary the coloring.

Now I'm scattering fur card clusters across the skull surface using filtered normal directions so fur only grows on upper/front-facing areas, with the card orientation flowing down and back for a natural fur look. I'm working out the arm and leg placement by looping over left/right sides, computing shoulder and hand positions symmetrically based on a sign multiplier for each side.

Writing the limb and chain code...

Computing finger joint positions...

Checking the finger overlap at the sprig radius confirms slight embedding, which is good, and both hands wrap symmetrically from the sides. Now I'm setting up the leg geometry, defining hip and foot positions and building the limb with knee offset outward for correct sign on each side.

Setting up leg chains and foot/toe geometry...

I notice the toes are floating away from the branch surface rather than hugging it—I need to reposition the toe path points relative to the branch axis so they wrap tightly against the branch radius instead of leaving a visible gap.

Defining branch curve points...

Checking sprig radius and position against the hand and body geometry to make sure the twig placement looks natural against the koala's belly and limbs.

Now I'm positioning the sprig leaves further up so they clear the fingers, keeping only the upper cluster of leaves and adjusting the count to avoid overlap with the hand.

Adding another branch curve...

I'm also planning gumnuts on two of the twigs and sketching a stub with a cut end near the trunk base.

Then I'm working out the sweep path and radius for the trunk itself, making sure its top connects cleanly where the branch begins.

For bark stretching I'll use directional scaling depending on orientation—horizontal streaks stretched along x, vertical trunk stretched along y, keeping twigs more isotropic. Then I'm laying out the base as textured planks using a tiled wood texture box, tinted appropriately, and considering adding edge trim strips around the base.

Adding corner nail heads as tiny dark boxes at the four top corners, plus metal corner brackets with bolts for detail. I'm embedding a plaque box into the front face with the texture centered and slightly recessed, then scattering several moss patch boxes across the top of the base at varied positions.

Now I'm placing a few gray pebble spheres, then laying down flat leaf litter cards on the base surface with randomized rotation and mirroring so they look naturally scattered.

For the body fur, I'm scattering tuft cards across the surface with distance constraints and normal/height filters, then narrowing further so the gray tuft placement avoids blending into the cream belly area.

Now I'm adding a second cream-colored tuft pass for the belly, plus smaller tuft scatters on the arms, legs, and ear tips to match proportions. Then I'm setting up the pixel-art eye texture palette.

Writing plank texture generator...

Writing the build function...

Adding bark knot embedding options and small box-geometry bark plates along the branches, then I'm ready to finalize the description and write the file.
